title: Why Does Your FUNNY BONE Hurt So Much? ⚡
description:
You bang your funny bone on a door frame and your whole arm goes ZAP. It's not funny, and it's not a bone: it's a nerve with nothing over it but skin. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

How it works: the ulnar nerve is one of the main nerves of your arm. It runs from your neck to your fingers, tucked under muscle nearly all the way. The exception is your elbow, where it passes round a knob of bone in a shallow groove, right under the skin. A knock there squashes the nerve itself against the bone, so instead of a bruise you get an electric zing, and you feel it where that nerve ends: in your little finger and the near half of your ring finger. The knob belongs to the bone of your upper arm, the humerus. Humerus, humorous: that may be where the name comes from, or it may simply be the funny feeling. Nobody knows for sure. The zing fades in seconds; tingling or numbness in those two fingers that stays is one for a doctor.
